newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police threw Berlin hijacker out of plane - witness.
newsitem.headline: Police threw Berlin hijacker out of plane - witness.

text.p: German police commandos ended Tuesday's hijacking of an Austrian Airlines plane in Berlin by sneaking in at the rear and pushing the hijacker out of an open front door, an eyewitness said.

Passenger Thomas Taeubner, 43, told reporters at Berlin's Tegel airport that the hijacker had been standing in the open doorway and was pushed out. Taeubner said the man, reported to be a Bosnian, fell about five to seven metres (yards) to the tarmac.
"The police entered from a rear entrance and they were able to surprise the hijacker," Taeubner said. "They pushed him out the front door."
Taeubner said the hijacker appeared to have suffered scrapes from the fall. Police could not immediately confirm the account.

Taeubner, a Berlin resident flying to Vienna, told a group of journalists that the special commandos were wearing black ski masks. He said the hijacker had been sitting in a row immediately in front of him, was carrying a knife that appeared to be about half a metre (20 inches) long.
